title: OperationalProfileResult
description: Structured operational-profile research answer for a prospect's fleet and port footprint, in the marine fuels and shipping-services lens (Poseidon Phase 8, doc 02 section 4.3 -- the new-prospect brief's research subskill, first call). Minimal v1, ITEMS-SHAPED BY DESIGN (Task 2's own resolved judgment call -- see fixture_tool.py's module docstring and the Task 2 report): vessel types, preferred ports, and operational notes are each represented as one item, distinguished by the item's own category field, rather than as three separate top-level arrays -- this keeps the schema's TOP-LEVEL shape identical to sustainability.json/market_position.json/strategic_profile.json/web_research.json (items[] + summary), so the shared poseidon.mcp.perplexity.adapter.validate_and_normalize pipeline needs no schema-specific branch to normalize this schema's responses. Versioned by filename, matching web_research.json's own convention.

items.description: Individual vessel-type, preferred-port, or operational-note findings, ordered by relevance as returned by the model. See this schema's own top-level description for why these three concepts share one array instead of three.

category.description: Which operational-profile bucket this item belongs to: a vessel type operated, a preferred/home-base port, or a free-form operational note.

label.description: Short name -- the vessel class (category=vessel_type), the port name (category=preferred_port), or a short heading (category=note).

detail.description: Descriptive detail -- typical use for a vessel type, usage context for a port, or the note body.

relevance.description: Why this item matters to a marine fuels and shipping-services sales conversation.

summary.description: A short overall synthesis of the fleet and port footprint, in the marine fuels and shipping-services lens.
